# dsh-whale-dive
Read **Bilibili** and **Douyin** from inside DeepSeek Harness: nine model-facing tools, two very dif
ferent transport problems, one read-only surface.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why two transports
**Bilibili** answers plain HTTPS — but it signs its newer routes with a rotating `w_rid` (the "WBI"
scheme) and it answers a sustained burst with an **IP-scoped HTTP 412 that outlives the burst by min
utes**. Measured on one machine: 20 threads × 10 requests passed cleanly; 8 threads of mixed `view`+
`search`+`reply` for 30 seconds (≈51 req/s) produced 1372 × HTTP 412 out of 2128 requests, and the b
lock was still in force 90 seconds later. So the plugin ships a pacing layer rather than a bare `fet
ch`: a token bucket keyed per host, a concurrency cap, and a circuit breaker whose cool-down doubles
on each consecutive trip.
The same measurement run also showed which routes survive without a signature, so the plugin prefers
those and keeps the signed route as the fallback:
| Route | Signed? | Read by |

| `x/web-interface/view` | no | `bili_video` |
| `x/web-interface/popular` | no | `bili_feed` (popul

ar) |
| `x/web-interface/related` | no | `bili_feed` (related) |
| `x/v2/reply` | no | `bili_comment

s` |
| `x/player/v2` | no | `bili_subtitles` |
| `x/v1/dm/list.so` | no | `bili_danmaku` |
| `x/web-

interface/card` | no | `bili_author` (profile) |
| `x/relation/stat` | no | `bili_author` (counts) |

| `x/series/recArchivesByKeywords` | no | `bili_author` (uploads, default order) |
| `x/web-interfa

ce/wbi/search/type` | WBI | `bili_search` |
| `x/space/wbi/arc/search` | WBI | `bili_author` (upload
s, explicit order) |
**Douyin** cannot be read over HTTP at all. Its API calls carry `a_bogus`, `X-Bogus` and `__ac_signa
ture`, all computed at runtime inside an obfuscated VM, and a plain client gets 403s, empty bodies,
or a captcha interstitial. Headless browsers get the captcha too. The only route that works is a rea
l, headful Edge/Chrome whose page computes its own signatures — so `whale_dive_douyin` launches one
in its own profile directory, drives it over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, and reads the rendered DO
its own profile directory, drives it over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, and reads the rendered DOM.
That path costs several seconds per call, and one detail is not obvious: a window parked off-screen
is treated by Chromium as occluded, and an occluded window stops painting — the feed never hydrates
and the DOM stays empty. The launcher therefore passes `--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows`, `
--disable-renderer-backgrounding` and `--disable-background-timer-throttling`, which is what makes t
he parked window actually render.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`, so the loader row is inserted for you. Nothing else in
the composition is touched: no base row config is replaced, no search provider is registered, so th
is patch cannot collide with another plugin that selects a provider.
Restart DSH after installing — profile changes are picked up at startup.
## Configuration
All fields live under the plugin's settings section and are read on every tool call, so an edit appl
ies to the next call without a reload.
| Key | Default | Meaning |
| `requestsPerSecond` | `4` | Per-host request rate. The measured safe band is 5–10 req/s; 4 leaves

headroom. |
| `burst` | `8` | Token-bucket capacity — how much idle time can be spent at once. |
| `

maxConcurrent` | `3` | Requests in flight at one time. |
| `cooldownMs` | `120000` | How long one ri

sk signal parks a host. Doubles per consecutive trip. |
| `maxCooldownMs` | `600000` | Ceiling for t

he doubling cool-down. |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | Per-request timeout. |
| `cookie` | `""` | A `SES
SDATA=...` string. Only needed for subtitle bodies and the handful of routes that answer `-101` with

out a session. |
| `douyinBrowser` | `""` | Explicit path to Edge/Chrome. Empty auto-detects. |
| `d

ouyinPort` | `47821` | DevTools port for the helper browser. |
| `douyinUserDataDir` | `""` | Profil

e directory. Empty uses a temp directory. |
| `douyinKeepAliveMs` | `900000` | How long an idle help

er browser stays alive. |
| `douyinWaitMs` | `11000` | Settle time after `loadEventFired` on Douyin.

Not padding — the feed hydrates asynchronously. |
| `danmakuLimit` | `500` | Default cap on danmaku

rows. |
| `commentPageSize` | `20` | Default comment page size. |
## Douyin sign-in (optional)
`hot` and `feed` need no account. Keyword search does: Douyin gates it behind a login wall and shows
"登录后即可搜索更多精彩视频" to anonymous visitors. To unlock it, run `whale_dive_douyin` with `action: "video"`
once — this starts the helper browser — then scan the QR code in the window that appears. The sessi
on is stored in the plugin's own profile directory (never your normal browser profile) and reused af
red in the plugin's own profile directory (never your normal browser profile) and reused afterwards.
## Output conventions
Two rules run through every tool:
- **A field is only ever omitted, never invented.** When a surface is gated, the tool still *succeed
s* and explains the gate in `note`, because "this is gated and here is the way in" is a useful answe

r and a thrown error is not.
- **Every number is coerced.** Upstream sends `null`, missing keys and
`"1.2万"`, all of which would violate the output schema; each is projected to a typed value before th
e harness validates it.
Rate-limit failures are the exception: they throw an `HttpError` with `code: "RISK"` and `risk: true
`, carrying the cool-down window. That distinction is deliberate — a model that reads "intercepted,
stop calling this host" behaves differently from one that reads "request failed" and retries into a
g this host" behaves differently from one that reads "request failed" and retries into a longer ban.
## Requirements

- DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.1 < 0.3.0-0`
- Node `>= 20` (the Douyin path uses the global `WebSocket`)
- Micro
soft Edge or Google Chrome for the Douyin path; the Bilibili path needs neither
## Scope
Both backends are read-only. Nothing here posts, likes, follows or writes.
